profiles.name: Yuma Test Center UAS and Counter-UAS Testing

before.overview: Yuma Test Center hosts developmental UAS and counter-UAS testing, including 2026 multi-vendor exercises and permanent evaluation lanes. Army reporting identifies private customers paying test costs and a West Cibola initiative intended to accelerate industry testing. Users should pursue the named Army customer process; this is not an unrestricted public range.

after.overview:
Yuma Test Center supports developmental UAS and counter-UAS evaluation in a military range environment. Army reporting describes dedicated evaluation lanes for sensing, electronic effects and kinetic engagement, with instrumentation and test methods for comparing performance under realistic conditions.

Private companies can enter through the Army range-reservation concierge for the West Cibola initiative. Customers pay the costs of their testing, and submitting a request does not guarantee the preferred site or schedule. Bring a test objective, system description and safety requirements; confirm permitted effects, airspace, sponsorship or contractual conditions and current availability with the range. This record is not permission to fly or conduct mitigation.
after.contact_text: Army test-range concierge for commercial test requests; scope, range assignment, safety approvals, costs and schedule are agreed with Army staff.
after.test_aircraft: Uncrewed aircraft and counter-UAS evaluation; specific aircraft, emitters and effects require range approval.
after.test_dimensions: Military range environment with instrumented evaluation lanes. No customer-specific operating boundary or aircraft limit is established by this profile.
after.test_access: Apply through the Army test-range concierge. Private customers fund their tests; access, safety requirements, permitted effects and scheduling require approval and are not guaranteed.

sources.supports: Commercial concierge route, customer-funded testing, private-industry access initiative and no guarantee of location or timeline.

before.overview: Christman Airfield is CSU's named flight facility in Fort Collins. The university describes UAS testing and training alongside crewed aviation and research use, with collaborations involving educational, industry and government users.
before.test_access: CSU states that all UAS and general-aviation activity requires prior Drone Center approval and all users must complete annual safety training.

after.overview:
CSU's Christman Airfield supports UAS testing, flight operations, training and research, with a published 4,000-foot asphalt runway suited to fixed-wing work. The operator also lists weather reporting, Remote ID/ADS-B monitoring and research collaborations with educational, industry and government users.

All UAS and general-aviation activity requires CSU Drone Center approval. Reservations need at least 48 hours' notice and users complete annual airfield safety training; additional insurance, radio and other requirements depend on the activity. Submit the aircraft and proposed mission before arranging a visit. Site waivers and FRIA status are operator-described reference information, not transferable permission for a customer's flight.
after.contact_text: CSU Drone Center for aircraft testing, partner research and advance airfield reservations; annual safety training and operator approval apply.
after.test_aircraft: UAS and crewed general aviation; published runway supports fixed-wing activity subject to operator acceptance.
after.test_dimensions: 4,000-foot asphalt runway with runway lighting; weather reporting and aircraft/UAS monitoring.
after.test_access: Prior CSU Drone Center approval for all operations; at least 48 hours' reservation notice and annual airfield safety training. Confirm activity-specific insurance, equipment and aviation approvals.

sources.supports: 4,000-foot runway, supporting systems, prior approval, annual safety training and minimum 48-hour reservation notice.

profiles.name: ACT Aerospace Gunnison Composite Structures Facility

before.overview: Aerospace composite structures, machining, tooling and assembly production.

after.overview:
ACT's Gunnison operation supports composite aerospace structures from part/tool design and analysis through fabrication, machining, assembly and inspection. Published services include mechanical material testing, environmental testing and ultrasonic/non-destructive inspection, making this a potential resource for prototype structures and production components rather than only a general company listing.

Bring drawings or CAD, materials, load cases, tolerances, quantities and qualification requirements to the sales/project team. Agree the manufacturing and inspection plan, current capacity, evidence required for the part and any export/customer restrictions. The manufacturer's published equipment list does not by itself establish a qualification for a particular unmanned aircraft or open access to its factory.
after.contact_text: ACT published company inquiry email and Gunnison phone for composite part design, tooling, fabrication, assembly and inspection quotations.

profiles.name: Bush Combat Development Complex Innovation Proving Grounds

before.overview: BCDC's IPG page describes mobility courses, off-road areas, urban/subterranean settings and integrated communications for scenario-driven assessments. It supports testing of autonomous ground vehicles, air-ground teaming and resilient networks with government, industry and academic partners.

after.overview:
The Innovation Proving Grounds at Texas A&M-RELLIS combines a one-mile mobility challenge course, off-road terrain, configurable urban buildings and subterranean environments for scenario-based evaluation. The operator describes air-ground teaming, communications/cyber testing, instrumentation, live/virtual integration and test-planning support.

A government, industry or academic team can scope mobility, perception, teaming or resilient-network experiments with BCDC. Define vehicle dimensions, terrain, communications, hazards, instrumentation and data needs before requesting access. The published BVLOS corridor and other facilities are project-planning leads, not blanket aircraft acceptance or permission to fly. Confirm the exact available areas, agreements and aviation approvals for the proposed test.
after.contact_text: BCDC published leadership/project-coordination route for scoped test planning; site and aviation access require agreement.
after.test_aircraft: Autonomous and crewed ground platforms, air-ground teaming and communications experiments; aircraft acceptance is project-specific.
after.test_dimensions: One-mile mobility challenge course, off-road areas, configurable urban structures and subterranean test environments.
after.test_access: Scope the experiment with BCDC, including platform, hazards, instrumentation, data and site requirements. Confirm agreement, scheduling and any airspace authorization; published corridors do not grant flight permission.

sources.supports: One-mile mobility course; off-road, urban/subterranean, network, instrumentation and test-planning capabilities.

before.overview: ModalAI provides integrated perception and communications hardware for aerial and ground autonomy. Its contact page publishes a San Diego address and separates technical-support forums from sales inquiries. It is useful as an onboard autonomy electronics and integration supplier.

after.overview:
ModalAI supplies compact onboard computing, flight-control and perception hardware for autonomous drones and ground robots. Its VOXL 2 platform combines edge compute and an autopilot with a software/tooling ecosystem for visual-inertial navigation, mapping, obstacle avoidance and object recognition; sensors and communications modules are selected as part of the configuration.

Developers can start with documentation and development kits, then take interface, camera, compute, power, radio and software requirements to sales/application support. The published product page distinguishes hardware and software lifecycle versions. A listed Blue UAS component does not certify every finished aircraft, software build or mission; confirm the complete configuration, availability and integration scope.
after.contact_text: ModalAI sales/application inquiry for autonomy hardware and integration; use the linked technical forum/documentation for support rather than treating the office as a shared flight-test lab.

profiles.name: DeTect Panama City Radar and Counter-UAS Systems

before.overview: DeTect develops radar and related surveillance products for detecting and tracking small UAS and other targets. Its Panama City operation is a specific supplier contact for airspace-awareness and detect-and-avoid integration. Product detection claims do not establish permission to fly BVLOS or employ counter-UAS effects.

after.overview:
DeTect develops radar and surveillance systems for airspace and maritime awareness, including small-UAS detection and tracking. Its HARRIER and DroneWatcher portfolios are relevant to site surveillance, airport awareness and integration of drone activity with other detected targets; these are product/system capabilities, not a declared open-access evaluation range.

A facility operator should discuss the detection problem, terrain and coverage, target characteristics, alerting, network integration and installation/support needs with the company. Confirm a site survey, actual performance assumptions and permitted equipment before procurement. Detection capability or a counter-UAS product label does not confer authorization to jam, intercept or destroy aircraft.
after.contact_text: DeTect's published company contact route for surveillance-system requirements and site integration; no countermeasure-use authority is implied.

profiles.name: University of Michigan Mcity Test Facility

before.overview: UMTRI identifies Mcity as an early-stage development facility with roads, intersections, connected infrastructure and remote as well as on-site testing. Its current description also mentions expanded electric/uncrewed aerial testing with M-Air. Teams can investigate repeatable connected/automated-vehicle research and testing; this is not a general public-road operating permission.

after.overview:
Mcity is a controlled early-stage mobility test facility with a 32-acre site and more than 16 acres of roads and traffic infrastructure. Published features include urban/suburban road scenarios, a 1,000-foot straightaway, connected infrastructure, mixed-reality testing and remotely accessible research tools. The current operator page also describes low-altitude UAS support, which must be scoped separately from ground-vehicle tests.

External users execute the track agreement and provide liability-insurance evidence before booking. Safety orientation applies to participants, and access is restricted to approved testing/research teams. Discuss vehicles, scenarios, support equipment, data and any aircraft needs with the facility manager; a track booking does not provide public-road or flight authorization.
after.contact_text: Published Mcity Test Facilities Manager Jim Lollar for track/research inquiries. The office phone is general coordination; agreements, insurance and safety orientation still apply.
after.test_aircraft: Connected/automated ground vehicles; UAS and low-altitude test support are described by the operator and require project-specific confirmation.
after.test_dimensions: 32-acre facility with over 16 acres of roads/traffic infrastructure and a 1,000-foot straightaway. Ground-track dimensions are not runway specifications.
after.test_access: Closed research/test facility. External users need a track agreement, approved liability-insurance evidence and booking; participant safety orientation is required. Confirm separate UAS and support-service arrangements.

sources.supports: Facility/road dimensions, connected/remote testing, low-altitude UAS support, track agreement, insurance and safety orientation. The live page names facility manager Jim Lollar and publishes his project-inquiry email.

profiles.name: ATI Industrial Automation Apex Robotic Sensing and Tooling

before.overview: ATI develops robotic sensing and tooling that lets robots measure and respond to physical contact. Its Apex engineering team and published radiation-tolerant sensor offering are relevant to manipulation and remote operations in hazardous environments. This is a component and integration supplier, not a mobile-unmanned-system manufacturer.

after.overview:
ATI supplies robotic force/torque sensing, tool changing and end-of-arm tooling for controlled contact and automated production tasks. Its radiation-tolerant sensor offering is relevant to manipulation and inspection in hazardous environments, while its material-removal application guidance supports defining robot processes such as finishing and machining.

A robotics or manufacturing team can request component/application support with robot payload, tool loads, required sensing range, mounting, environment and process details. Confirm the selected sensor/tool's qualification and integration, rather than assuming every product is radiation-tolerant. This is a component supplier, not a complete autonomous vehicle or a bookable robot test cell.
after.contact_text: ATI/Novanta application engineering for robot tooling and material-removal process scoping; the official application sheet publishes an engineer inquiry email.

Contact partnerships with the operating problem, environment, desired outcome, constraints and deployment economics. NREC publishes indicative project stages and durations, but cost and schedule need a current project-specific estimate. Agree data, intellectual-property licensing and commercialization arrangements; the partnership process is not general public access to laboratory equipment.
